title: Birthright is one of the most thoughtful and nuanced plays I’ve seen ...
transcript: I think you would have a hard time finding a Jewish person that doesn't have a complicated feeling about birthright. Birthright being the free 10 day trip to Israel you get just for being Jewish. It's also the name and topic of the three hour and 20 minute epic currently playing at MCC Theater for full transparency. I went on birthright in 2011. I went by myself with a bus full of strangers and came back with good friends and a lot of questions. So I found myself immediately relating and reacting to this play. Birthright is written by Jonathan Specter, who wrote one of my favorite plays, Eureka Day and follow six friends who met on birthright over nearly 30 years of friendship. What Jonathan does so well is he really embraces complexity and gives so much room for nuance and difficult conversation. And if you are a Jewish person in 2026, you have had so many of these conversations with your Jewish friends and with your family, and it can feel so isolating and so tense. And I just felt so seen the reality of loving people who will just never understand your viewpoint and the pain that comes along with that. I was invited to opening night, which was so fun. We left the theater and immediately had a Jewish feast and also great people watching. Now, if you're going to see birthright, you should know it does have some nudity and they do use yonder pouches. Meaning your phone does stay with you, but it's off and locked in a bag, and there are no photos or videos anywhere in the theater. But there are two intermissions, and you can get your phone unlocked in the lobby. I really did love birthright so much. I thought the cast was phenomenal. You completely believe that they have been friends for decades, and you will leave this theater with a lot to think about. Birthright is currently playing at MCC through July 26th. I'm so glad this play is in New York right now.
classificationReason: First-hand review of Birthright at MCC Theater. Creator attended opening night, names the playwright (Jonathan Specter), discusses the show's nuance, and shares strong personal emotional reactions to the production.
